允 has permission and sincerity associations. In 允可 いんか, it contributes permitting or assenting. This is a useful recognition word for formal or older writing, not the default way to ask permission in conversation. The source classifies 允 as a name-use character; that does not make every use a personal name.

The modern shape has 厶 above two leg-like strokes, 儿, the indexing radical. Modern-shape mnemonic: picture someone standing beneath a sign granting permission. This is a visual memory aid, not a historical derivation or a phonetic analysis.

All four sourced readings remain in their original order, but reading questions select only イン. The historical office-title use of じょう is real, not merely a personal-name reading. The last two rows preserve dictionary lookup information without inventing modern word spellings. The dot in まこと.に is the source's okurigana notation; ゆるす is preserved without a dot.
For the everyday verb "allow; forgive," learn 許す ゆるす. Its written form and range of meanings are not automatically transferable to 允.

元, "origin, former," has two horizontal lines above its legs; 兄, "older brother," has a square 口. Neither has 允's upper 厶 shape.
去, "leave, elapse," has 土 above 厶 rather than 厶 above 儿.
許, "permit; forgive," overlaps in meaning, but these are not interchangeable spellings in every word.
Name readings are outside this card's practice scope. Do not use the quiz subset as a complete guide to reading personal names.

允可 means permission or assent: accepting a request or allowing something. It is a noun and can form a transitive verb with する. Learn it primarily for recognizing formal or older writing, rather than as a default conversational request.
允可を得る (いんかをえる) - obtain permission.

This pattern is attested in an 1868 governmental text cited by Nikkoku; it is shown here in dictionary form, not as a quotation of the whole historical sentence. 允可 is the permission obtained; を marks it as the object of 得る (える), "obtain." The example does not mean "give permission."
JMdict also glosses the word as "compliance." Read that with the surrounding request or permission context, not as a universal substitute for every kind of obedience.
允 contributes permitting or assenting, and 可 contributes approval or acceptability. The near-synonymous parts reinforce the permission idea. The on readings are イン + カ, giving いんか.

許可 (きょか), "permission; authorization," is a more practical general-purpose word for permission. 許す (ゆるす) can mean "allow" but also "forgive"; 允可 does not automatically cover that entire range. 承認 (しょうにん), "approval; recognition," can overlap in an approval context. There is no single everyday antonym that fits every permission or assent situation.

Recognizing this word does not mean you need to use it in ordinary conversation. For example, 写真を撮ってもいいですか (しゃしんをとってもいいですか), "May I take a photograph?", asks for permission without using 允可. Nor is 允可 restricted here to one legal procedure or permission from an emperor: the dictionary definition is broader than any one historical example.
